title: Cannelloni di Carne
subtitle: Pasta tubes filled with beef and ricotta in tomato and béchamel
excerpt: Pasta tubes filled with a seasoned beef and ricotta mixture, baked under a double covering of tomato sauce and béchamel. Assembled ahead and baked from the fridge, they are an ideal meal for company.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cannelloni, the name means large tubes, is a pasta format used across southern Italy and in the Italian diaspora. The dish was popularised internationally in the twentieth century and became a staple of Italian-American cooking. The filling of meat, ricotta, and egg bound together is standard in the Neapolitan tradition; northern Italian versions often use a different ratio or add spinach.

content.text: Filling cannelloni tubes is easier with a piping bag or a sturdy sandwich bag with a corner snipped off. The filling should be firm enough to hold its shape, if it is too wet, add more parmesan or a spoonful of breadcrumbs. The dish can be assembled the day before and refrigerated, then baked from cold with an extra 10 minutes added to the cooking time.

Make the tomato sauce: fry the onion in olive oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic for 2 minutes, then the tomato puree for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, season, and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.

Make the filling: brown the beef in a dry frying pan over high heat for 5 minutes until well coloured. Season and leave to cool. Combine with the ricotta, half the parmesan, and the egg. Mix well and season.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk gradually over medium heat. Stir until thick. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Spread half the tomato sauce in the baking dish. Fill the cannelloni tubes with the meat mixture using a piping bag and lay over the sauce. Spoon the remaining tomato sauce over the tubes, then cover completely with béchamel. Scatter the remaining parmesan over the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
